extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and administrative staff preparing NIH grant applications (e.g., K08) and documenting facilities/resources and biosketches
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing the 'Facilities & Other Resources' and Senior/Key Person Profile/Biographical Sketch sections for an NIH grant application, documenting institutional infrastructure, core services, equipment, data security, and required biosketch components and formatting limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental administrative support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Surgery will provide the administrative support for this research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List departmental offices and staff (e.g., Research Office, Accounting Office) that assist with grant administrative pages, assurances/certifications, post-award accounting, and purchasing services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical core support for study design
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statistical Analysis/Research Programming Core provides comprehensive statistical support for study design and grant application through selection of outcome variables, statistical analysis planning, power analysis and sample size calculation, and random assignment of treatment conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document availability of full-time biostatisticians/programmers and their role in protocol design, power calculations, and randomization planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of statistical methods available
rubrics_metrics.description: Statisticians perform research hypothesis testing and data analysis using a variety of statistical methods including but not limited to ANOVA, Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, Generalized Linear Model, Survival Analysis (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank test, Cox models), Nonparametric Statistics, Meta-Analysis, Longitudinal Data Analysis, Multilevel Modeling, Structural Equation Modeling, Data Mining, Machine Learning, Model Selection and Variable Selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which advanced and domain-appropriate statistical techniques are supported and available to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical interpretation and clinical translation
rubrics_metrics.description: The statisticians also interpret the analysis results and translate statistical significance to clinical implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate statistical collaboration includes interpretation and assistance in converting results into clinical context for manuscripts and presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and psychometrics evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Statisticians will evaluate psychometric properties of measurement instruments including survey questionnaires, assessing reliability, validity, factor structure, and performing item and test analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document capacity for instrument validation and psychometric analyses when measurement tools are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database management and analytic dataset preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Statisticians provide database management, maintenance, patient cohort extraction, and analytic data set preparation, especially for projects using large national health outcome databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe database capabilities, cohort extraction procedures, and who will prepare analytic datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript and presentation assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The statistical analysis core can provide feedback for peer-reviewed publications and oral and poster conference presentations, including description of statistical methods, generation of results summary tables and figures, and reviewing and editing of manuscripts, abstracts, and presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note editorial support scope (tables/figures generation, method descriptions) and inclusion on manuscripts as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and training on software and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Statisticians provide consultation and training on study design, data creation and management, statistical analysis methods, and statistical software programs (including SAS, SQL, Stata, R, SPSS, and Matlab).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List training offerings and available statistical software environments that investigators can access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure computing infrastructure and data protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Department computing features modern Windows-based devices with access to a fully managed, secure, high-speed infrastructure physically secured within a data center and logically secured with a next generation firewall; all data are protected using an off-site secure data storage facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe physical and logical security, off-site backups, and general infrastructure protections for research data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical security controls for data center
rubrics_metrics.description: Only members of the SMPH IT staff have physical access to the secure data center; access is controlled by individual key card access and pin number; all entries are logged and cameras record activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document who has physical access, access logging, and surveillance measures for spaces holding sensitive research data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity, authorization, and HIPAA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Users must apply for and be approved for access by Department human resources; accounts are fully HIPAA compliant, with password complexity requirements and expiration policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm account approval workflows, HIPAA-aligned authentication and password policies for users handling PHI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access management and change control
rubrics_metrics.description: Users have unique accounts; rights to files/folders can be audited; access control lists are only editable by IT staff and changes are only made under authorization of the Principal Investigator or data custodian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe role-based access, change authorization (PI/data custodian), and auditability of access rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit controls and regular access review
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators and data custodians can perform regular review of access to systems and data storage folders and files, in collaboration with Surgery IT staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify frequency/process for access reviews and availability of access logs for audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of statistical application servers and software
rubrics_metrics.description: The statistical application server hosts SAS, STATA, and SPSS applications with flexibility to add other products as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List hosted software provided centrally and note flexibility to install additional analysis tools required by projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized computational resources and redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: A centralized computing facility provides secured, fault tolerant servers, database servers, web application servers, desktop clients, integrated storage with redundant file servers, RAID storage and tape backup systems with offsite storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document server counts, storage capacity, redundancy measures (RAID, mirrored storage), and backup/archival procedures supporting research computing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data backup and archival practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Data are backed up each night to a large tape library, and all data are archived monthly, both on-site and offsite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe backup frequency, archival schedule, and offsite storage arrangements to ensure data integrity and recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core facilities access and shared instrumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators have access to core facilities (Histology Core, Confocal Core, Flow Cytometry Facility) and shared equipment (e.g., qPCR, centrifuges, microscopes, ELISA readers, flow cytometers, cryostat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List available cores, major instruments, booking/billing software (e.g., iLab), and analysis packages provided on-site (FlowJo, IDEAS, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal facility accreditation and services
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal care facilities are AAALAC and NIH approved, directed by licensed veterinarians, offering purchasing, housing, animal care, sentinel monitoring and euthanasia; animal care and use protocols are approved by the UW Animal Care and Use Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State accreditation status, veterinary oversight, available animal surgery/procedure rooms, and existence of approved IACUC protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory space, equipment, and bench resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The lab contains all the major equipment and bench space necessary for the proposed project, is highly collaborative, and includes items such as laminar flow hood, incubators, microscopes, PCR systems, centrifuges, freezers, liquid nitrogen tank, and PC workstations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an inventory of PI lab equipment, bench space, and proximity to colleagues who can share equipment and expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity and availability of surgical/microsurgery facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Small animal surgery can be performed in microsurgery laboratories equipped with stereomicroscopes in the WIMR Vivarium; a one-way procedure room equipped with anesthesia machines and stereomicroscopes is located adjacent to the PI’s lab space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document availability, equipment, and adjacency of operative procedure rooms needed for the project's in vivo work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and tele/videoconferencing support
rubrics_metrics.description: Services include WisLine teleconferencing, HSLC videoconferencing rooms with audio-visual equipment and staff support, interactive high-definition portable systems, and Cisco Webex subscription for internet-based collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe available conferencing systems, capacities (room sizes), staff support for connections, and institutional subscriptions used for remote collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental technical, editorial, and administrative staff support
rubrics_metrics.description: Department employs biostatisticians, microcomputer technicians, an editor, medical librarian, full-time accountants and financial specialists, pre-award and editorial staff, medical illustrators, IT technologists, copy machines, and hospital shops to support research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerate administrative and technical staff available to investigators for grant preparation, manuscript editing, IT/user support, financial management, and in-house fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Clinical Research trial support services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides comprehensive support for interventional clinical research trials including activation, budgeting and contract negotiation, IRB submissions, enrollment/consenting, data collection and subject-follow-up; staff obtain certification in Human Subjects Research, Good Clinical Practice, and HIPAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail clinical trial management services available, staff composition (regulatory specialists, coordinators, nurses), and required certifications held by staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional translational research resources (ICTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICTR offers research methods courses/workshops, informatics tools, biostatistical and regulatory support, research software, and core technologies to link basic research to community practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe institutional translational resources, training opportunities, and cross-school/core collaborations that support translational aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch formatting and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required sections (Personal Statement; Positions and Honors; Contribution to Science; Research Support), education/training table, and adhere to the five-page maximum per biosketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Person Profile required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: RESEARCH & RELATED Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) PROFILE - Project Director/Principal Investigator: fields include Prefix, First Name, Last Name, Position/Title, Organization Name, Department, Division, Address, Country, Phone Number, E-Mail, Credential (eRA Commons), Project Role, Degree Type, Degree Year, Attach Biographical Sketch, Attach Current & Pending Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all mandatory form fields in the Senior/Key Person Profile and attach biosketch and current & pending support documents as required by the application form.
